title: Courses and Service
short: Wait until everyone is served or the host begins; at a large table, start when the host invites you. Food is traditionally served from the left and plates cleared from the right.
trouble: Learners start as soon as their own plate arrives at a dinner party. At a large table the host may say "please start while it's hot," and then it is polite to begin.

blocks.html: A formal setting tells you the order of the courses. Service, the way food is brought and taken away, has its own customs, and so does the moment you begin to eat.
Wait until everyone is served or the host begins; at a large table, start when the host invites you. Food is traditionally served from the left and plates cleared from the right.

Starting together means nobody eats alone while others watch, and the host sets the pace for the whole table. Serving from one side and clearing from the other is a working rule: servers do not collide with each other or reach across a guest's eating hand, and guests learn to lean slightly the other way.

opts.narr: With eight at the table, the host invites the guests who are served first to begin.

blocks.title: Served first
blocks.q: At a dinner party for ten, Ruby is served first. The host is still in the kitchen. What should she do?
steps: Wait: starting alone while others watch is the slip.
Keep her hands in her lap and talk with her neighbors.
If the host says, "Please start while it's hot," she may begin.
blocks.a: Wait for everyone, or for the host's invitation.

blocks.title: A server at your side
blocks.q: At a banquet, a server approaches James's left side with a platter. Then later a server comes to his right. What is happening?
steps: Food is traditionally offered or served from the left.
Plates are traditionally cleared from the right.
James leans slightly away from the server and says thank you.
blocks.a: Serving from the left, clearing from the right.

blocks.name: et-order
blocks.cap: An informal menu. At a formal dinner, a fish course may follow the soup and the salad may follow the main course.

blocks.html: Starting as soon as your own plate arrives at a dinner party. Wait for the others or for the host. At a large table the host may say "please start while it's hot," and then it is polite to begin: the invitation is the signal.
Customs differ: in some families everyone waits for a blessing or a few words from the host; in others, the oldest person begins. Follow the host's way.
